statements.venue: Joint statement with Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester, published as a press release
statements.quote: work through solutions that maintain America’s competitive edge in development while ensuring that these technologies serve human interests and remain fully under human control. In the meantime, Congress must ensure necessary safeguards are in place.
statements.context: Curtis and Blunt Rochester, both on the Senate Commerce Committee, called for immediate public hearings with AI developers to inform possible AI regulation.
statements.reason: Saying AI must 'remain fully under human control' and needs safeguards acknowledges a serious risk in general terms, but the statement names no catastrophic outcome and does not say control could be lost, so it sits between C and D.

notes: Seven web searches ran (six required plus one repeat of the official-site search, because the first returned only unrelated results); none was refused. The quote was read on curtis.senate.gov and copied by script from the page text (it uses a curly apostrophe in America’s). It is a joint statement by two senators, not Curtis alone. A reviewer should decide whether 'remain fully under human control' earns C or D. No source found showing Curtis co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (reported as introduced by Sen. Sanders and Rep. Casar); he is not on the verified signer list of the 23 September 2026 China letter. The Deseret News and KSL articles (16 September 2026) only repeat fragments of the same statement. Not opened: his chatbot child-safety and data-center press releases (out of scope), and the Semafor 16 September 2026 report on bipartisan AI safety talks, so any role for Curtis there is unchecked. No hearing remarks, floor speeches, op-eds or interviews by Curtis on catastrophic AI risk were found, but the search was limited and cannot rule them out.
